text:
Brett Howden's season is a depth forward's quiet upgrade. He has six goals in 21 games for Vegas without a single power-play point, and the real change is the quality of his looks: 1.16 expected goals per 60 on his own shots (a measure of chance quality), against 0.62 last season. Six goals on 6.24 expected means nothing in the finish is borrowed.

The points around him have dried up, two in his last ten games, but our numbers put that more on his teammates' finishing than on his play. Vegas has scored 4.6 fewer goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice, which usually swings back. He kept shooting in Friday's shootout loss to Nashville (five shots) and scored against Utah two nights earlier, "Brett Howden through traffic," as Jesse Granger of The Athletic put it. NHL EDGE counts 55 bursts over 20 mph, 92nd percentile, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him getting 1.6 shots per 60 off passes across the slot or from behind the net last season. Watch whether the chance rate holds; it's the part of his game that's different.
headline: Brett Howden's chances are new, and they look real
